prerequisites: Foundational knowledge in computer science (Boolean algebra)
Basic notions of Physics, with emphasis on electricity, resistors, capacitors, circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts of electrical circuits.
Understand the basic concepts of semiconductor devices.
Understand the concept of amplification and main operational amplifier applications.
Understand the concept of logical inverter and its performance.
Understand the basic digital CMOS circuits.
Understand the different types of semiconductor memories.
Be able to analyze electrical circuits under DC and transient operation.
Be able to analyze basic diode circuits.
Be able to analyze circuits with operational amplifiers.
Be able to analyze basic CMOS digital circuits and the mutual constrains arising from their interconnections.

Be able to autonomously judge the adequacy of a particular component for digital circuits to satisfy assigned specifications expressed through the main and most common performance metrics for digital circuits.
Be able to communicate in Italian with third party experts in the sector regarding the functions and performance of digital circuits
Ability to learn how new digital circuits work and compare them with those learned in the course.

syllabus_topics: Electrical circuits: generators (voltage/current, indipendent/controlled), resistor, capacitor, parallelel/serier connections, Kirchoff's laws, Thevenin's and Norton's theorems. Electric power.
Inverter: operating principle (ratioed, static, dynamic), figures of merit, power consumption.
CMOS circuits: combinational and elements of sequential logic circuits.
Semiconductor memories: operating principles of ROM, OTP, static and dynamic RAM and non volatile flash memories.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (theoretical questions and simple exercises)

assessment_rules: The final written exam includes theoretical questions and simple exercises, organized into two parts (one for basic circuit analog and one for digital electronics topics). Each part is 1 hour and has 4-7 questions/exercises. The maximum score is 33 points, and the evaluation considers the gravity of errors and the class's average performance.
bibliography: J.M. Rabaey, A. Chandrakasan, B. Nikolic. Circuiti integrati digitali, seconda edizione, Pearson/Prentice Hall, 2005. (also available in english edition, useful for the digital electronics part)
N. Storey. Electronics-A system approach, Fifth edition, Pearson, 2013. (for the analog electronics part)
